articles.title_orig: Wisconsin police find dozens of partially clothed men in frat house basement in alleged hazing incident
articles.title_zh: Wisconsin police find dozens of partially clothed men in frat house basement in alleged hazing incident
articles.content_orig:
Two 20-year-olds were arrested after police were called to the scene of an alleged hazing incident where over two dozen young men were partially clothed and covered in liquids. Some of them were injured, police said.
The Madison Police Department said they received an anonymous tip about an event at the unaccredited Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity. When they arrived at the house, they found about 30 "partially clothed males covered in food, condiments and other liquids" in the basement. The room's thermostat was set to 81 degrees, police said.
Several of the men had "visible injuries consistent with being abused," police said.
The "vast majority" of the men were 18, police said.
A photo with the men's faces redacted shows the group in a dirty space with black walls and the Alpha Epsilon Pi letters painted on a piece of furniture.
Two people, identified by police as Brayden J. Klein and Samuel N. Vane, were arrested for hazing and disorderly conduct and taken to the Dane County Jail. The Madison Police Department said that the president and vice president of the fraternity were present and spoke to responding officers, but did not specify if Klein and Vane held those titles.
The men in the basement were escorted outside and checked for incapacitation and injuries.
"Several of these men had visible injuries consistent with being physically assaulted," police said.
No other charges have been announced in relation to the incident. An investigation remains ongoing, and those with information are asked to contact the Madison Police Department.
Alpha Epsilon Pi is an unrecognized and unaccredited student organization at the University of Wisconsin, police and the school said. The school said in a statement that because the chapter is still recognized by the national Alpha Epsilon Pi organization, it is legally allowed to operate as an unaffiliated fraternity chapter.
A spokesperson for the Alpha Epsilon Pi Headquarters said it takes the allegations concerning the Madison chapter "extremely seriously." The national organization plans to "cooperate fully" with the investigation, the spokesperson said, and members found responsible for criminal conduct will be expelled from the organization.
"Hazing is a betrayal of everything our fraternity stands for," the spokeperson said." There is no place for it in AEPi. No exceptions. No excuses. We educate our members about their responsibility to 'Be Your Brothers' Keeper.' This is not an optional value. It is a fundamental expectation of membership. Anyone who engages in hazing forfeits the privilege of being an AEPi brother."
The University of Wisconsin said it is also investigating the incident as it relates to its nonacademic misconduct process. Campus officials are providing support to affected students.
The Madison Police Department said that anyone whose safety is jeopardized during the Greek life recruitment process should contact authorities.

articles.title_orig: Treasury Yields Are Spiking. Where to Invest in the Bond Market Now.
articles.title_zh: Treasury Yields Are Spiking. Where to Invest in the Bond Market Now.
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Treasury yields inched higher on Friday as recent selling pressure intensified following hawkish Fed commentary and stronger-than-expected economic data.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury note was up more than 2 basis points to 5.183% after reaching its highest rate since June 2007 on Thursday. The 30-year Treasury bond was higher by more than 1 basis point at 5.476% after surging to levels not seen since 2004. The 2-year note yield was up less than 1 basis point at 4.901%.
One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
Investors weighed a global bond selloff this week as Japanese government bonds, U.K. gilts, German bunds and other eurozone bonds hit fresh highs. Eurozone and Japanese government bond yields edged lower on Friday.
Treasury yields have been driven higher by hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr, who said in a speech on Wednesday that "further policy adjustments" can be expected to bring inflation down to target. Other factors included stubbornly high oil prices and the purchasing managers' index report hitting its highest level in more than four years.
Traders were last pricing in a 66% chance of a rate hike in October, according to the CME FedWatch tool .
On Friday, the Commerce Department reported that durable goods orders in August were relatively unchanged. Economists polled by Dow Jones had expected a decline of 0.3%.
"Ahead, we think that there are enough rate hike fears discounted at this juncture, and certainly enough to take care of perceived inflation risks," ING's regional head of research for the Americas Padhraic Garvey and senior rates strategist Benjamin Schroeder wrote in a note on Friday.
"But, government bond yields are primed to remain under pressure on a pure debt dynamic theory, which translates into pressure for some re-widening in swap spreads, and especially in the 10yr area."

A nor’easter is set to slam the East Coast over the weekend, dumping heavy rain and unleashing hurricane-force winds on residents living in North Carolina all the way up to Maine.
Forecasters warn of major coastal flooding, dangerous surf and strong rip currents as the storm takes shape off the coast of North Carolina Thursday before its set to head north over the weekend. The inclement weather will coincide with a full moon, which will contribute to high tides and coastal flooding.
“This storm may be remembered for its destructive coastal flooding and severe beach erosion, especially along eastern Long Island and the Massachusetts coast,” AccuWeather Chief Meteorologist Jon Porter said.
Strong wind gusts topping 40 mph from North Carolina to New York are pushing ocean and bay waters toward shore, and meteorologists say flooding will be at its worst through Friday in the mid-Atlantic region.
The most significant flooding will be from southern New Jersey to the northern Outer Banks of North Carolina, according to The Weather Channel.
Water levels are expected to rise 2-3 feet above the average monthly tide level, with some areas seeing water go six feet above that level. The worst flooding is expected in Virginia’s Chesapeake Bay, according to AccuWeather.
Southeastern New England will see the heaviest rainfall, with the brunt of the storm expected to hit from Friday night through Saturday night in parts of Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New Hampshire and Maine.
Some urban areas like Boston may even see flash flooding, forecasters warned.
However, damaging winds may pose an even greater threat to the region, as forecasters say gusts could reach hurricane-force and cause trees to topple and take down power lines.
“Many trees still have their leaves, which catch more wind and place additional strain on their roots, further increasing the risk for trees to come down and may also increase the number of power outages as compared to similar storms,” Porter said.
Meteorologists also warned that heavy rain from last week has left soil moist, increasing the likelihood of trees being uprooted by strong winds.
Periods of heavy rainfall may also lead to flooding. Forecasters predict rainfall will total 1-2 inches from northeastern New Jersey to coastal Maine, while central Massachusetts to the coast will see anywhere from 4-8 inches.
Forecasters warned the storm could take on some characteristics that resemble a tropical storm.
"Given that the developing nor'easter will be slowly moving over the very warm water of the Gulf Stream for two or three days, the storm may take on some characteristics that would resemble a tropical storm. Such hybrid storms are called subtropical storms," Porter said. "Regardless of classification, the storm will be impactful, especially for coastal areas."

articles.title_orig: ICE wasted millions of taxpayer dollars in rapid push to expand detention capacity, government watchdog finds
articles.title_zh: ICE wasted millions of taxpayer dollars in rapid push to expand detention capacity, government watchdog finds
articles.content_orig:
In a single day in January, Immigration and Customs Enforcement spent more money than it had on any other day in either of President Trump's terms, federal spending records show.
The agency advanced billions to Chicago Title Insurance in escrow to acquire detention facilities, according to a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson. Over the next two months, ICE used $1.07 billion of the funds to purchase 11 warehouses it planned to convert to detention megacenters, seven of which the agency now plans to sell.
The rest of the money sat with the firm for months after ICE abandoned the warehouse plan. In July and August, ICE moved $2.2 billion from Chicago Title to purchase four detention facilities from CoreCivic, a private prison company it separately pays to continue operating them.
In its rush to expand detention capacity, ICE wasted millions of taxpayer dollars, the Government Accountability Office found in a report released Thursday. The agency failed to account for long-term costs in acquiring detention centers and lost $20 million in unrecoverable costs purchasing the warehouses it no longer plans to use, the review found. Even more could be lost if ICE sells the warehouses for less than what it paid for them, the GAO report said.
Barring any undisclosed purchases, $1.55 billion still sits with Chicago Title Insurance for acquiring detention centers as ICE continues its push to double the number of detention beds in service of the president's mass deportation agenda. Just this week, ICE awarded several companies contracts that could reach a combined $10 billion to expand and construct new facilities.
GAO concluded that "urgent planning" is necessary to reduce further waste. ICE said it would produce a strategic plan by Aug. 31, 2027, a date the watchdog said wasn't soon enough.
"We just saw a real lack of planning overall," said Heather MacLeod, director of Homeland Security and Justice at GAO. "The lack of planning has really led to stops and starts which have ultimately resulted in waste."
GAO's report did not estimate a total amount potentially lost to waste, but MacLeod said another review of ICE spending is currently underway.
Flush with cash after Congress funneled $75 billion to the agency — including $45 billion to expand detention capacity — through President Trump's " One Big Beautiful Bill Act ," ICE has nearly doubled its spending this year. The agency spent $19 billion from last October to July, the most recent month for which data is available, up from $11 billion the previous full fiscal year, a CBS News analysis of federal data found.
A DHS spokesperson wrote to CBS News that ICE is "working at turbo speed on cost-effective and innovative ways to deliver on the American people's mandate for mass deportations of criminal illegal aliens," and that the spending bill known as OBBBA has provided "historic funding" to help it carry out the mandate.
Appropriating funds outside of the typical process — and without the usual guardrails that come in appropriations bills — means ICE has more flexibility in how it can use the funding, said Kevin McNellis, a policy and budget analyst who previously worked in the Congressional Budget Office and Congressional Research Service. That also leads to a breakdown in oversight, he wrote in a report he authored for Co-Equal, a nonprofit focused on congressional authority.
"When DHS only had annual funding or relied on the annual appropriations for the majority of its funding, there were long standing systems and processes in place for DHS to inform Congress of its spending plan and for Congress to then oversee those spending plans," McNellis told CBS News. "The situation we've been in since OBBBA passed is we have an unprecedented amount of money, appropriated outside those long-standing processes, trying to be spent very quickly."
ICE paid an 11% to 13% premium on the 11 warehouses it purchased, according to CoStar, a real estate analytics firm. Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem directed ICE to purchase new detention sites within 30 days, contributing to the high prices, The Wall Street Journal reported .
The remaining warehouses ICE still hopes to convert face legal challenges, though ICE already signed contracts worth a combined $426 million to renovate two of them. No detainees are currently held in any of the warehouses.
After dropping the warehouse plan, ICE spent $1.47 billion purchasing two California detention facilities from CoreCivic in July. The next month, ICE bought another two CoreCivic facilities in Kansas and Minnesota for a combined $734 million. In its announcement of the August purchases, CoreCivic said the company is in talks with ICE to sell more facilities.
CoreCivic is using the profits from the sales to pay down its debts, according to company filings .
GAO found that ICE had only forecasted costs for these centers and to-be-converted warehouses for the next three years, failing to consider how it would pay for them once the funds Congress has allocated through 2029 run out.
The watchdog also found that through FEMA reimbursements, ICE paid the state of Florida almost triple its typical per-bed rate for two state-operated facilities, including the now-shuttered facility dubbed "Alligator Alcatraz." ICE skipped typical contract negotiation practices, creating a new grant program with the state of Florida as the only eligible recipient, according to the GAO report. FEMA paid Florida a total of $608.4 million for "Alligator Alcatraz," GAO said.
ICE is also paying more than it typically would per-bed to house noncitizen detainees at facilities operated by the Bureau of Prisons. BOP officials told GAO they've had to pay staff overtime and for temporary assignments to meet ICE's needs, resulting in a per-bed-rate double that of ICE's median rate.
Another abandoned initiative GAO cited was ICE's efforts to launch detention facilities at military bases, like the one at Camp East Montana in El Paso. A previous GAO review found ICE spent $7.1 million on detainee meals it did not need at the El Paso facility. ICE dropped its plan to launch similar facilities on military installations in Indiana and New Jersey, GAO reported.
ICE also spent $2.85 million on tents at Guantanamo Bay to house detainees that were never used. The facility, initially planned for 30,000 detainees, held only a handful. In May, CBS News reported that the Guantanamo Bay facility was holding just six detainees. The agency is still trying to house detainees on the naval base: this week it signed a contract with the same company it used to help procure the warehouses and acquire the CoreCivic facilities to construct a facility at Guantanamo Bay and at other sites.
DHS's Inspector General is conducting its own audit into ICE's acquisition of detention space to determine whether it made purchases in a "cost-effective manner." The internal watchdog is also probing ICE spending on air charter services and its reporting on how it is using Big Beautiful Bill funds.
"We think it's important that DHS and ICE do develop a plan going forward tied to their needs and what they're trying to get out of their expansion efforts," said MacLeod, the GAO director. "We're encouraged to see that they agreed with our recommendation and we're hoping they'll take steps to address it quickly."
Sophia  Vlahakis contributed to this report.

The prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, who leads the far-right Brothers of Italy party, said her government had approved what she called “commonsense measures that do not divide but genuinely help to integrate”.
Writing on social media, she said the measures included:
“A limit of 30% in classrooms for students who do not adequately know Italian, plus tools to learn our language and a halt to burqas and niqabs in school.”
The announcement was a toned-down version of comments she had made earlier in the week at an event organised by Brothers of Italy’s youth division.
“It cannot be that in the classroom it is Italian children who feel left out because they’ve become the minority,” Meloni said as she vowed to “legally set the number of foreign students per class”.
Thursday’s decree also sets out that in cases where students show persistent problems with integrating or struggling to learn the language, their parents will be referred to social services and will have to take free literacy and Italian language classes. Parents’ failure to comply could result in fines of up to €1,000.
The education minister, Giuseppe Valditara, said the measures, set to take effect in the 2027-28 school year, would affect about 1,000 classrooms, or about 0.3% of the total nationwide.
Rights campaigners were swift to link the measures to next year’s election, in which Meloni’s premiership is facing an unexpected challenger on the right.
“ She’s creating an emergency that is not a real emergency at all, ” said Daniela Ionita , of the campaign group Italians Without Citizenship, pointing out that an estimated 60% of the pupils who could be described as foreign were born in Italy but faced a myriad of hurdles when it came to accessing citizenship.
“Because there are now new parties pushing from the right, I think Meloni is scared, ” she said.

articles.title_orig: Inside NBC News’ polling averages: Democrats enjoy biggest lead yet in the race for Congress
articles.title_zh: Inside NBC News’ polling averages: Democrats enjoy biggest lead yet in the race for Congress
articles.content_orig:
Democrats are heading into the final stretch of the 2026 midterms with their largest lead yet in the race for Congress and President Donald Trump’s approval rating at a significant low, according to NBC News’ newly released polling averages.
A 9-percentage-point advantage for Democrats when it comes to control of Congress is part of a steady deterioration of the political environment for Republicans. The parties started the road to this November effectively tied in the weeks after President Donald Trump returned to office last year, but independents have gradually begun to prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress. And those voters have soured on Trump and his economic policies in particular.
The congressional average, which stands at 52% to 43% after adjusting to a likely voter scale, measures whether Americans prefer a Congress controlled by Democrats or Republicans before things like individual races and candidates come into play.
Individual polls can bounce around, but an average gives a broad sense of where surveys are trending, and it controls for outliers, which is one reason NBC News released our averages now. At a time when a flurry of polling is released, such as in the homestretch of an election cycle, averages can be valuable tools for tracking what’s happening in the election and diving deeper into how Republicans, Democrats and independents view Trump and the battle for Congress.
The NBC News averages are weighted calculations of all publicly available polls that meet certain standards for methodology and transparency tracking back to the beginning of the second Trump administration.
Our polling averages are designed to measure changes in public opinion over time, rather than reflecting the result of any single survey. They combine national polls using a statistical weighting method that gives greater influence to the polls that are most informative while reducing the effect of random variation from individual surveys.
Every polling average makes methodological choices about which polls to include and how much influence each should have. This methodology is used for both the NBC News presidential approval average and the generic congressional ballot average.
While the underlying calculations differ slightly to reflect the characteristics of each type of polling, the overall approach is the same.
Our approach emphasizes five principles:
Averages are not predictions. Instead, they aim to provide the clearest possible aggregate measure of the current available polling.
Polls of all adults, registered voters and likely voters are all eligible for inclusion, as are polls with a partisan affiliation provided those surveys meet certain methodological transparency requirements. Polls with partisan affiliations are noted as such whenever possible. NBC News collected all the surveys included in the average.
To be eligible for inclusion in the average, a polling organization must, at minimum, meet methodological transparency standards by reporting details on when a poll was conducted and how many respondents were interviewed. If a poll does not publicly release information on field dates, sample size and/or margin of error, it is not included.
Not every poll contributes equally to the average. Older polls gradually receive less weight as new surveys are released. Likewise, polls with smaller sample sizes or larger margins of error contribute less than more precise surveys.
Check out the full methodology page for the NBC News poll averages here .
With a month to go before the midterm elections, Trump’s approval rating has slid to 39% in the NBC News polling average , with 59% disapproving of his job performance so far. He began his term at 50% approval, according to the average.
There has been little change over time among partisans in the race for Congress, with the vast majorities of Republicans and Democrats standing with their parties consistently.
As a result, much of the shift toward a preference for a Democratic-controlled Congress can be explained by the changing preferences of political independents.
Independents preferred Democrats by about 6 points at the beginning of Trump’s second term, and they slowly moved toward Democrats toward the first half of last year. But things began to shift more rapidly during fall 2025 and early 2026, moving to a lead of about 20 points for Democrats in the spring — as public frustration with Trump’s handling of the economy, the war in Iran and the killings of two Americans by federal immigration officers began to boil over.
The Republican Party hasn’t fully recovered with independents since, and Democrats now hold a 16-point lead among those voters in the race for Congress, according to the average. While survey responses don’t automatically translate into election results, such a strong showing among political independents is one of the many encouraging signs for Democrats heading into the election.
Even so, it’s no guarantee of electoral success for Democrats as Republicans seek to find a way to energize the coalition that sent Trump to the White House just two years ago and narrow the gap before Election Day, more than a month away. Republicans also hope they can defy the political headwinds because so many of the key battleground House and Senate races are being fought in districts and states Trump won in 2024, some by double-digit margins.
For Trump, movement among independents — and Republicans, to a lesser extent — explains his low marks from voters.
His approval rating among Republicans fluctuated in the mid-to-high 80s for the first six months of his second term, but now, his GOP approval rating is at 79% in a slight but noticeable decline, according to the average.
Independents’ approval of Trump has dropped further, to 26% in the NBC News average.
Voters have specifically soured on his handling of two of his signature issues — the economy and border security and immigration. In April 2025, an NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey found 40% of American adults approved of Trump’s handling of inflation and the cost of living, while 60% disapproved. By this April’s poll, 32% approved and 68% disapproved.
Every polling average reflects decisions about which polls to include, how much influence to give them and how to account for differences in whom pollsters survey and how they go about it.
Some polls survey all adults in the U.S., which includes people who aren’t registered to vote or who aren’t eligible to be registered, such as recent immigrants. Other polls specifically survey registered voters.
A third set of polls — which become more frequent as the clock ticks down to Election Day — are polls of a population that pollsters identify as likely voters. Likely voter polls try to capture the attitudes of the group of people who will actually cast ballots, a moving target for polling organizations given the impossible task of predicting voter turnout exactly.
Those three sample universes produce slightly different results on our two key questions. Polls of all adults consistently show a lower approval rating for Trump compared with polls of registered or likely voters. Likely voters are likelier to have made up their mind on the generic ballot question about control of Congress, and as a result, both parties receive higher vote shares among that group.
Both our presidential and congressional averages combine those three universes by adjusting polls of adults and likely voters so they are on the same scale as registered voters. However, because the congressional ballot preference is a question about how people will vote, the congressional average shifts to show a likely voter baseline after Labor Day.

articles.title_zh: ‘Gonzo bonkers’: Trump’s plan to militarize triumphal arch sparks pushback
articles.content_orig:
Democratic Sen. Tammy Duckworth of Illinois is demanding the Pentagon and Federal Aviation Administration reject President Trump's call to convert plans for a massive triumphal arch into a "top grade Military Complex" equipped with snipers and with the capability to store, launch and land drones while in the flight path of Washington's Ronald Reagan National Airport.
"The FAA and DoD must reject this foolhardy plan and instead focus on increasing the safety of the airspace," Duckworth, who lost both legs while serving in the Iraq War, wrote in a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford.
The FAA determined last week that the 250-foot arch, which is being constructed near Arlington National Cemetery, poses no hazard to flights coming into and departing from Reagan Airport.
The letter was exclusively obtained by CBS News. She called Mr. Trump's announcement, made in a Truth Social post over the weekend, "bizarre, unhinged early morning social media rants."
In the letter sent Friday, Duckworth, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Subcommittee on Aviation, Space, and Innovation, took Trump administration officials to task for "wasting time, energy and taxpayer dollars on yet another Trump vanity project."
She called it "particularly outrageous" after what she described as the "joint failure" of the FAA and Defense Department "to effectively implement corrective actions that were recommended" by the NTSB following the January 2025 midair collision near Reagan Airport that killed 67 people.
The NTSB made 52 safety recommendations following the collision between a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter and an American Airlines regional jet that was landing at Reagan Airport.
Thirty-five recommendations were directed to the FAA, only three of which have been closed. The NTSB said earlier this month the FAA's responses to 11 of the recommendations were unacceptable. All 13 recommendations directed at the Pentagon remain open.
"It is disturbing to see Federal officials devote enormous attention to an unnecessary, proposed structure while the NTSB and the public are still demanding action on recommendations intended to prevent another catastrophic collision in our skies," Duckworth wrote. "The American people cannot afford to stand witness to Trump's risky plan to place a 250-foot structure along a busy approach path, especially if he follows through on plans to station snipers on the arch and fly drones ... in the already congested airspace."
While calling the FAA's review of the proposed arch "incomplete," Duckworth, a former Army helicopter pilot, is demanding answers to a host of questions, including if the FAA considered the use of the arch as a military complex during its safety assessment.
She is also calling for Hegseth to disclose "which military entity, if any, requested that the arch be converted into a 'Military Complex,' and what threat assessment supports that request?"
She requested answers by Oct. 5.
In a statement earlier this week, Democratic Rep. Don Beyer of Virginia wrote that "putting a drone launching site directly in the landing path for DCA is a stupid, dangerous, and unworkable idea."
The FAA and Defense Department declined to comment on the arch, referring inquiries   to the White House.

The Iran war is driving fuel prices higher worldwide, leading to angry protests around the globe and straining the economies of countries that have nothing to do with the war.

Yes, but: Price increases vary greatly from country to country.
Context: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries are also helping to boost motor fuel prices, especially diesel.
The big picture: With no resolution to the conflict in sight, many governments face hard choices — strain their budgets with fuel support or face the political consequences of higher fuel costs.
State of play: Dozens of nations have taken steps to cap, subsidize or lower taxes on various fuels, per the International Energy Agency. Governments are also taking steps to reduce demand, such as more remote work and limiting government travel.
What they're saying: "Many places have failed to reduce demand and are instead artificially constraining prices," said Joseph Webster, an energy scholar with the Atlantic Council.
Zoom in: Rising fuel costs are compounding existing inflation, public debt and youth unemployment problems in Kenya, Carnegie Endowment for International Peace scholars wrote in late August.
"Kenya's case serves as a signal for others in the region caught downstream of the war's economic blow," they write, arguing for greater "resilience" measures that make nations less vulnerable to external shocks.

Danish intelligence officials have warned that Russia could launch a "limited" military attack against a NATO member in the coming months, saying the Kremlin appears more willing to take risks after more than 4½ years of war against Ukraine.
The Danish Defence Intelligence Service, or DDIS, on Thursday identified a "low but growing risk" that Russia could carry out isolated strikes with long-range weapons on infrastructure that is critical to the support of Ukraine.
"A limited military attack would be a desperate move on Russia's part and, like the intensified hybrid attacks, could potentially take place in the coming months," it wrote in a report.
"The purpose would be to redirect European resources away from supporting Ukraine and to sow division within NATO, should the alliance fail to agree on a collective response."
The DDIS added that it saw no indications that Russia would launch an outright invasion of a NATO country, although it said it could not rule this out.
Russia could also deploy a limited number of troops, possibly without national insignia, into NATO countries on its border, the DDIS said. However, it said that such a buildup would be difficult to conceal and take several months to prepare.
The new threat assessment joins a chorus of Russia warnings from top European security officials and lawmakers in recent days.
NATO members that border Russia are Finland, Norway and Poland as well as the Baltic states of Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania.
Poland's government on Thursday said a blaze at a Starlink ground station in the country was an act of sabotage aimed at disrupting internet services, including for Ukraine's military.
Poland's deputy prime minister, Krzysztof Gawkowski, said it had not yet been established who was responsible for the fire, but "many signs suggest this aligns with Russia's new ‌doctrine ⁠of attack," according to Reuters .
A spokesperson for Russia's embassy in London was not immediately available to comment when contacted by CNBC. The Kremlin has previously denied involvement in similar incidents.
Denmark's intelligence service also warned that Russia will intensify its hybrid war by carrying out more attacks against the West and NATO, "with greater consequences for the targeted countries than in the past."
These could include major cyberattacks that seriously damage vital societal functions as well as sabotage attacks with a high risk of casualties, the DDIS said.

“We can’t let external noise divide us,” Kraft said. “Us guys in this locker room, we’re really all we’ve got. We spend a lot of time together, so just continue to stay close and build off each other.”

Boors the world over once insisted that no one watches women’s sports. Now, grown men are trying to declare for the WNBA draft. That should illustrate just how popular women’s basketball has become over the last few years, buoyed in part by an insurgent class of superstars.
Made possible by the historic CBA that was signed in the eleventh hour of the off-season, the WNBA’s 30th anniversary season has been must-see TV. This year, the league welcomed two new expansion franchises—the Toronto Tempo and the Portland Fire—and a generational talent in rookie Olivia Miles, not to mention boatloads of new fans. And for the first time ever, the WNBA’s All-Star game was better-attended than the NBA’s.
Despite what the sensational headlines might lead you to believe, there has never been a better time to be a fan of the WNBA. The hoops, too, are as competitive as ever—league-wide parity means that any team can be beat on any given night. Case in point: the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx won only six more games this season than the eighth-seeded New York Liberty , who they’ll play in the opening round when the playoffs begin on Sunday.
As someone who grew up watching the NBA, I’ll admit that it took me a few years to get accustomed to the flow of the women’s game. But diving deeper into the WNBA, and sitting in the upper bowl of a sold-out United Center at the WNBA All-Star Game in July, has brought back the kind of pure excitement and curiosity I felt when I first fell in love with basketball as a kid.
So, here’s a pro-tip for any WNBA newbies: instead of allowing right-wing panic about trans athletes to dictate your experience of the W, try actually watching the games. (Better yet, get to one in person). Trust me, the hoops (and the vibes) will not disappoint. What follows is a comprehensive guide to the WNBA postseason, tailor-made for fans who may only just be coming around to the beauty and ferocity of women’s basketball.

In this economy, it wouldn’t be wise to bet against the Las Vegas Aces. The reigning champs are seeded third, behind the Minnesota Lynx and the Golden State Valkyries, But the Aces are experienced and well-oiled, led by Becky Hammon and a staff of hoodie-blazer-wearing coaches who know exactly how to get their team playing their best basketball when it matters most. Oh, they also have four-time MVP and three-time DPOY A’ja Wilson , who every year strengthens her case for being the greatest player in league history. Leading the league once again in points and blocks, Wilson wisely opted to remain stateside to recover from a nagging back injury instead of competing in the FIBA World Cup. If the Aces continue playing the way they did in the final week of the regular season, they may well win their fourth chip in five years. To get in the mood, run back A’ja’s fadeaway game-winner during game three of the 2025 Finals as time expired. Absolute cinema.
Rookie Olivia Miles came into the league and commanded immediate attention. The 23-year-old star, dubbed “the Spectacle” by fans in reference to her nifty play and the goggles she wears on the court, was drafted into the perfect situation under the guidance of Head Coach Cheryl Reeves (who’s coached and won four championships with the legendary Maya Moore). The fact that the Lynx finished with the league’s best record is notable considering the team only returned four players from the previous season, including All-Star Courtney Williams (½ of the StudBudz ) and former Defensive Player of the Year Napheesa Collier, who returned from injury midway through this season and continues to return to form.
Reeves has given Miles the ultimate green light to explore her fresh, uncanny brand of basketball in Minnesota. With one dribble, she can make defenders disappear from view. Her court vision is unmatched, too. Even perennial MVP candidate Collier said “she’s never played with someone” quite like Miles. Chances are you haven’t seen anything like her either.
At the start of the season, no one was checking for the Washington Mystics. Steadily and impressively, they’ve proven themselves. The self-proclaimed “Young Hos” of the league are the only other team besides the Lynx and the Aces to have defeated every playoff team in the regular season.
This will be the first playoff appearance for sophomore stars Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen. But watch out for the Mystics’ red-haired, fifth-year center Shakira Austin, who’s made a strong case for Most Improved Player as the team’s 26-year-old relative elder stateswoman. The Mystics play fearless and confident. And without the burden of high expectations, they’re primed to pull off an upset. “We cook on high heat, not on low heat,” Citron said. Translation? They aren’t waiting for permission to be great.
You might be wondering how the Valkyries can be considered a Cinderella candidate when boasting the league’s second-best record. But they’re only in their second season of existence, and the Bay Area expansion team led by Head Coach Natalie Nakase and General Manager Ohemaa Nyanin (former assistant GM of the New York Liberty) has become an absolute force, playing team ball on both sides of the court.
The Valkyries signed elite two-way All-Star Gabby Williams in the offseason to bolster a roster that’s mostly unchanged. In year two, the Valkyries have bought into playing a hard-nosed and stifling style of defense (they’re the number-one rated defense in the league) and also benefit from a deep and high-scoring bench. The big question, though, is whether Golden State will be able to win it all without a go-to bucket-getter to turn to in late game situations. If the Valkyries manage to pull off a championship in year two, a Bay Area parade might just generate enough good vibes to offset the bad juju coming from Silicon Valley.
This season, the noise around Caitlin Clark and her role-playing teammate Sophie Cunningham has been a massive distraction, to say the least. Clark got off to a slow start but kept shooting. Sure enough, in July, she had her breakout game, notching a career-high 45 points and 10 assists against Seattle. The game gave fans a glimpse of Clark at her very best, and she continued apace, ending the season averaging nearly 23 points a game.
Alongside her All-Star backcourt mate Kelsey Mitchell, Clark and the Fever are running the league’s most high-octane offense, with two of the W’s top three scorers (not to mention former first overall pick Aliyah Boston operating inside the paint). Last season, a Clark-less Fever took the Aces to four games in the semifinals; now at full force, they’ll be a very tough out.
In their first playoff appearance, the Paige Bueckers-led Wings will be missing key pieces, with 2026 number-one pick Azzi Fudd sidelined indefinitely after undergoing knee surgery. In their first season under first-time WNBA Head Coach Jose Fernandez, the Wings went from a 10-win team that missed the playoffs entirely to a 27-win team and the seven seed. Bueckers has put up MVP-caliber numbers all season long and is one of most enjoyable guards to watch on the planet. Plus, the Wings have nothing to lose. They won’t be going down easy if Bueckers and her fellow All-Stars Jess Sheppard and veteran Arike Ogwunbowale have anything to say about it.

articles.title_orig: Mikey Musumeci slammed hard at UFC BJJ but ultimately wins decision over Bryce Mitchell in main event
articles.title_zh: Mikey Musumeci slammed hard at UFC BJJ but ultimately wins decision over Bryce Mitchell in main event
articles.content_orig:
Mikey Musumeci had to endure a huge slam from Bryce Mitchell before winning a decision on Thursday
Mikey Musumeci came close on several submissions but the UFC BJJ champion was unable to put Bryce Mitchell away in their three round main event on Thursday night in Las Vegas.
The crossover match was set up as Musumeci has started to make his transition to a full-time MMA fighter and he showed off his skills without using any leg locks, which is one of his signature moves. Mitchell defended effectively over three rounds and despite not getting the finish, Musumeci had the time of his life.
“It was fun,” Musumechi said after the match. “I like that. I’m training MMA now so I like that. I want more MMA grappling opponents. I would prefer to do this style of grappling. It was way more fun for me.”
It took Musumeci just a moment to pull guard and he started pulling for leg locks, which got a few boos from the crowd after the competitors agreed on no leg locks. Musumeci did release the early hold. Musumeci again grabbed onto the leg as he went for the sweep and he quickly transitioned to an anaconda choke and then a power guillotine choke.
To his credit, Mitchell did a good job resisting the submission and eventually breaking free from the submission attempt.
On the restart in round two, Mitchell was able to get on top with Musumeci looking for an omo plata from the bottom. Musumeci stayed on his back trying to grab onto the arm or the head but Mitchell defended effectively as the match moved into the third and final round.
With Musumeci in guard, Mitchell was grinding his forehead into his opponent and then out of nowhere, the UFC bantamweight executed a huge slam that earned him a warning from referee Vitor Ribeiro.
This time, Musumeci executed a slick takedown of his own as he tried to set up a submission after taking the back. Musumeci had Mitchell in trouble after grabbing an arm but “Thug Nasty” stayed calm and composed to avoid the submission.
Mitchell bull rushed forward with another takedown before the match ended but to his credit, the UFC bantamweight held his own against one of the top grapplers in the world. Afterwards, Mitchell admitted he’d have to use punches to escape many of Musumeci’s best moves but they stuck to their agreement for the fight that ultimately lasted all 15 minutes.
There’s no word yet when Musumeci might actually take his first MMA fight now that he’s training full time at Syndicate MMA in Las Vegas but Thursday’s match proved that “Darth Rigatoni” is that much closer to his first official fight.

articles.title_orig: With Netanyahu at the U.N., Mamdani plants an olive tree with Palestinians
articles.title_zh: With Netanyahu at the U.N., Mamdani plants an olive tree with Palestinians
articles.content_orig:
Award-winning actress Susan Sarandon and Hacks star Hannah Einbinder were among dozens of protesters detained Thursday in New York during a demonstration against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as he visited the United Nations.
NYPD said it took 103 people into custody as it tried to break up a group participating in a sit-in protest on First Avenue, just a few blocks from the U.N. headquarters, ahead of Netanyahu’s remarks to the U.N. General Assembly.
Video from the scene showed officers zip-tying Sarandon and Einbinder’s hands and directing them toward an NYPD bus.
Meanwhile, protesters can be heard chanting with many wearing shirts that say, “Fund people not bombs,” and holding signs that say “Stop arming Israel” and “End the genocide.”
Comedian Caleb Hearon, author Glennon Doyle, New York congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier, and former Army intelligence analyst Chelsea Manning were also among those detained, according to Jewish Voice for Peace, a human rights organization that advocates for Palestinian rights and held the protest.
Video below: Netanyahu to NYC mayor Mamdani: "shame on you"
Other celebrities seen at the demonstration were actress and political activist Cynthia Nixon, playwright Tony Kushner, photographer Nan Goldin, and poet Eileen Myles. Congressional candidate Brad Lander also participated.
Jewish Voice for Peace said it held the sit-in outside the U.N. to “call on the world to stop arming Israel and to end the genocide in Gaza.”
A CNN team on the ground saw a heavy police presence with demonstrators remaining peaceful, but blocking traffic.
NYPD officers were seen arriving after noon and warned demonstrators to clear the street. Around 30 people remained sitting and standing on the street, the CNN team saw.
After another warning, officers began detaining protesters at around 1 p.m.
During his address Thursday, Netanyahu’s remarks prompted polarized reaction, with a large number of diplomats walking out of the room. The Israeli leader defended Israel’s military actions in Gaza and responded to international criticism, claiming if he hadn’t attacked Iran, “We’d all be dead.”
Last year, an independent U.N. inquiry found that Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza since Oct. 7, 2023, when Hamas carried out deadly attacks on Israel and Israel launched its military campaign. The Israeli government has maintained it is conducting the war in Gaza in self-defense and in accordance with international law, firmly denying accusations of genocide.
The International Criminal Court has issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu, former Defense Minister Yoav Gallantand a senior Hamas official, accusing them of war crimes. Netanyahu has dismissed the warrant as “absurd” and “antisemitic.” (The U.S. is not a member of the ICC)
After Netanyahu’s remarks, hundreds of protesters also marched through the streets of New York with some chanting “Free Palestine,” “Gaza,” and “Netanyahu, you can’t hide. We charge you with genocide.”
Sarandon has long-been a prominent supporter of Palestinian rights and has widely condemned Netanyahu and Israel’s war in Gaza.
In a story on Instagram , Hannah Einbinder acknowledged her detainment, writing, “If the pictures of my friends and me getting arrested in protest of Netanyahu’s shameful visit to New York draw attention to anything, let it be to the devastating genocidal war is waging against the people of Palestine and Southern Lebanon.”
Hearon also posted to Instagram , where he thanked the protest organizers and said he was out of jail.

articles.title_orig: Paramount Merger Settlement Won’t Be Resolved Until At Least Next Week As Judge Questions Agreement
articles.title_zh: Paramount Merger Settlement Won’t Be Resolved Until At Least Next Week As Judge Questions Agreement
articles.content_orig:
A coalition of groups under the Block the Merger banner have filed an amicus brief – a third party representation in a court case – opposing the Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger.
The brief was filed late Thursday by Free Press, the Committee for the First Amendment, the Freedom of the Press Foundation, the Future Film Coalition and the International Documentary Association in the federal court of California.
Earlier that day Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín, who is presiding over the case, gave interested parties permission to file amicus briefs with a deadline of 12:01 a.m. PT on Sept. 25 after the Block the Merger groups filed an emergency motion requesting leave to file. The legal move came after 12 state attorneys general reached a settlement over proposed legal action over the merger.
“Since the terms of the consent decree were announced on Monday morning, few outside of those with a financial interest in this deal have suggested that it addresses the harms to competition, creativity, and independent journalism this merger will cause for years to come. The deal has been met with silence, skepticism, or tepid support at best,” the groups said in a joint statement.
“The arguments laid out in this brief reflect the concerns that just days ago, California Attorney General Bonta also willingly voiced. While we may never know what caused the radical turnabout to deliver such a toothless settlement, we do know that this consent decree bucks governmental safeguards designed to protect the public from harm. The court should reject it outright.”
The League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) has also filed an amicus brief against the settlement.

articles.title_orig: US mortgage rates top 7% for first time in 20 months
articles.title_zh: US mortgage rates top 7% for first time in 20 months
articles.content_orig:
Increase comes after Fed decision to raise interest rates, as Americans struggle with high prices and stagnant wages
US mortgage rates surpassed 7% for the first time since January 2025, according to federal lender Freddie Mac, aggravating a housing market that has endured years of high interest rates and low supply.
The increase comes after the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates , which directly affect mortgage rates, for the first time since 2023, citing high inflation.
Rates on 16 September went up by a quarter of a point, to a range of 3.75% to 4%. In new projections, a majority of the Fed’s rate-setting committee predicted at least one additional rate hike before the end of this year.
Last year, the Freddie Mac 30-year-mortgage rate, commonly used on home loans across the country, had been trending down from 7.79% – a generational high reached in late 2023.
But rates have been creeping back up since late February, when the US and Israel launched its war with Iran . The conflict drove inflation to its highest levels in three years and sharply increased energy prices.
Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, topped $105 earlier on Thursday.
after newsletter promotion
On Thursday, the 10-year US treasury yield – which underpins the 30-year mortgage rate and other borrowing costs – also reached its highest level since July 2007 and the 30-year Treasury yield hitting its peak since 2004 as investors raised expectations for another Fed rate hike next month.
Earlier in September, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent announced the Treasury would triple its buyback of government debt, but yields have continued to rise.
The housing market has long been in a slowdown, said Anthony Smith, a senior economist at Realtor.com , with existing home sales hitting their 2026 low so far in August and pending sales that have turned negative year over year.
“A 7% handle is as much psychological as mathematical, and it arrives at the point in the season when leverage usually shifts toward buyers,” said Smith.
High mortgage rates are just one of the many reasons why Americans are struggling to attain home ownership. Wages have not kept pace with higher inflation, and everyday costs are higher.
The frustration is expected to show up in November’s midterm elections as Republicans struggle to maintain control of Congress. Nearly three-quarters of Americans disapprove of Donald Trump’s handling of the economy, according to a recent CNN poll conducted by SSRS , and two-thirds of registered voters rate the economy as “extremely important” to their vote.

articles.title_orig: Macron denies CIA warned France of Russian drone attack
articles.title_zh: Macron denies CIA warned France of Russian drone attack
articles.content_orig:
French President Emmanuel Macron denied CIA warnings of a possible Russian drone operation targeting southern Europe and pledged Thursday to send "military assets" to "protect" the Yanbu site, a key component of Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure network on Thursday.
In a joint interview aired on broadcasters France 2 and TF1 he said "We can deny this piece of information, the CIA did not inform France of this information and the Italian defence minister said the same thing".
On Thursday, Spanish daily newspaper El Mundo published an article which declared that the CIA had alerted several southern European governments to a possible Russian drone operation targeting Spain, France and Italy.
Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto subsequently denied these allegations on Thursday, declaring on X that "the alarm raised this morning by a Spanish newspaper that hypothesises possible attacks on Italy, Spain, and France by Russian ships and drones serves no one and is not confirmed."
"We already live in difficult, 'nervous' times, and no one needs more fuel on the fire", he added.
Macron also affirmed that France would send "military assets" to "protect" the Yanbu site of the East-West pipeline on the Red Sea, which provides Saudi Arabia with an alternative route for transporting crude and refined oil to European markets.
He detailed that this would amount to "military assets, meaning troops, radar systems, and defensive systems to protect this site, but we will not be engaging in any conflict. Our aim is to help stabilise the oil market."
The pipeline has played a crucial role during the war in the Middle East, allowing Saudi Arabia to bypass the Strait of Hormuz to export its oil. It can transport 5 million barrels of crude oil per day, with the capacity to temporarily increase to 7 million barrels.
The port, which also houses significant oil storage and refining facilities, has become a target for Houthi forces in Yemen, backed by Iran, during the current conflict in the Middle East.
"As soon as one of these locations is relaxed, the immediate impact is seen at the gas pump," the head of state added. "You'll see it in two days."
Hard-left France Unbowed leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon reacted to plans to mobilise military assets by calling for a parliamentary vote on the issue.
“Sending troops to Saudi Arabia means entering a theatre of war. If the base is attacked, what will we do? There’s no question of becoming a belligerent party," Mélenchon said.
Addressing Russia's ongoing and intensifying hybrid campaign against Europe, Macron referred to the drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport on the night of 4-5 August 2026, which German authorities have attributed to Russia.
Macron said France had not experienced a comparable attack so far but warned that one remained possible. "When you ask me, 'Could this happen?' my answer is yes," he said.
The French President stressed that Russia considers “Europe to be the strategic heart of Ukraine," while also saying that the possibility of Russia seeking to launch an attack against Europe was "plausible."
"It is clear that there have been several signs indicating that Russia is preparing to do this," he stated.
As speculation mounts over Russia’s possible mobilisation plans, Macron said that a new mobilisation of around 300,000 personnel was a “credible scenario” that was “often shared”.
The French leader said he viewed this as a sign that Moscow was prepared to "make even greater sacrifices to take over the entire Donbas", estimating that Russia would need to advance for “a year and a half, two years” at the current pace to conquer the territories it does not yet control in that region, “with terrible losses and suffering for Ukraine.”

articles.title_orig: Meta Launches $1M Developer Competition to Stock 'VR Glasses' with More Hand-tracked Apps
articles.title_zh: Meta Launches $1M Developer Competition to Stock 'VR Glasses' with More Hand-tracked Apps
articles.content_orig:
At Meta’s annual developer conference today, the company announced its next VR Start Developer Competition, this time slated to award a prize pool of $1 million to spark the community to get cracking on Meta VR Glasses-compatible content.
Meta is hoping to appeal to developers of both new and existing projects across entertainment, gaming, and productivity.
Notably, if developers are submitting games, they’ll be considering submissions in genres that work well for seated play, without controllers, such as puzzle, strategy, casual, social, and narrative experiences.
Games must be “fully usable with hands, end-to-end,” Meta says, noting that Touch controller support is welcome, but not required.
“For a small team without a marketing budget, that visibility drives traffic to your Store listing and gives you something concrete to point to when you pitch a new project or recruit collaborators,” Meta says.
This comes ahead of the company’s Meta VR Glasses announced at Connect this week, which does support Quest’s Touch Plus controllers, but doesn’t ship with them, instead putting its onboard hand and eye-tracking as its preferred control scheme.
Those are set to arrive sometime in Spring 2027, priced at $1,300. Check out our hands-on with Meta VR Glasses to learn more .
The competition takes place from today until November 18th, 2026, and is offering up prizes ranging in value from $20,000 to $100,000 for successful submissions. Winners will be announced on or around December 11th, 2026.
Since Meta VR Glasses run the same operating system as Quest, developers can prototype on Quest 3 in addition to using platform simulators like Meta XR Simulator ( Unity | Unreal ), Meta Spatial Simulator , and Immersive Web Emulator⁠ .
Interested developers can join the Start program now to enter for competition.

articles.content_orig:
It’s confirmed: The mysterious Motorola phone getting support for the privacy-focused GrapheneOS will be the Motorola Signature 27 that was announced earlier this week.
GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused take on Android that’s grown popular in recent years, has so far only been available on Pixel devices. That’s for a number of reasons relating back to how Google handles the software and the security components in Pixel (and Tensor) hardware.
But, now, GrapheneOS is officially stepping beyond Pixel and into a device that will come pre-loaded with its version of Android. It was announced that this would be a Motorola device, but which device was left a mystery as all existing Motorola devices were not compatible with the platform.
Unsurprisingly, though, the first GrapheneOS device from Motorola will be the Motorola Signature 27. GrapheneOS confirmed the news on Twitter/X , though other details are still minimal. It’s apparently still planned that devices will be sold with GrapheneOS pre-installed. The Signature 27 was announced earlier this week and its use of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset is likely a major part of the reason it will be able to run GrapheneOS properly.
An exact release date for the Motorola Signature 27 has yet to be confirmed, and it’s unclear if GrapheneOS will be available right away either. It’s already known that future versions of Razr flip and Razr Fold will also support the privacy-focused OS.

articles.title_orig: Google’s Gemini Can Now Make Calls for You on Pixel Phones
articles.title_zh: Google’s Gemini Can Now Make Calls for You on Pixel Phones
articles.content_orig:
Google has been trying to have its AI assistant make phone calls on your behalf for almost 10 years. Remember Duplex ? It enabled the now-defunct Google Assistant to call restaurants and book tables . That service was shuttered a few years ago, but now comes round two, powered by modern large language models .
On Thursday, Google announced Call for Me, an experimental beta feature exclusive to its latest Pixel 11 smartphones in the US (and in English). Pixel 11 owners need a Gemini subscription and have to be enrolled in the Phone by Google app’s public beta. Google has instructions on how to participate here .
These calls are designed to reach businesses. Gemini can call your local hardware store to ask if they stock a specific tool, or chat with a barber to schedule a haircut. Just tell Gemini to make the call—it may ask you follow-up questions for more context—and the chatbot will introduce itself and can have a back-and-forth conversation to ensure your request is handled. If it runs into an automated phone menu, it can navigate it and even wait on hold. On your end, you can view a live transcript on the Pixel and take over at any point.
Google says it works best with businesses, but there are some establishments Gemini won't call, like emergency services. That said, you can ask Gemini to call specific numbers. For example, if your tattoo artist doesn't have much of a web presence, “Gemini will try to search for a phone number, but you may provide one as well,” a Google spokesperson tells WIRED. During these calls, the assistant's voice will be the same one used in Gemini Live interactions , even if your preferred Gemini voice has an accent.
Call for Me expands on Google’s suite of smart calling features on Pixels and Android . The Phone app can already screen incoming calls and block robocalls and telemarketers. Hold for Me lets the assistant listen for when the hold music ends and a live person is on the other end; it alerts you to pick up the phone when it’s finally your cue. Direct My Call can display the different choices in an automated phone menu before they’re spoken, so you can tap nine to reach a live person and skip the recorded voice reading out the whole list. It even has real-time Scam Detection , alerting you when it thinks the person on the other end is scamming you.
Voice assistants handling phone calls is a little more accepted today than back in the Duplex days. Call screening features abound—whether on a Pixel, Samsung , or iPhone , onboard assistants routinely intercept unknown callers to ask why they’re calling.
But these kinds of features—much like hyped-up AI translation features—can often fall short. Calls are unpredictable, and the person on the other end may hang up, assuming it’s just another spam call. What happens if Gemini doesn’t understand a person’s accent all that well? Will it trap the clerk in an endless loop of asking them to repeat themselves? And if the shop doesn’t have the tool you need, does the bot know how to bow out politely—or just cut the line?
“That is exactly what we want to continue testing,” the Google spokesperson says. “With this experiment, we look forward to users testing a variety of cases, so that we can continue to improve the feature across accents and noisy environments.” And yes, Google says Gemini will “politely” hang up if the business can't accommodate your needs.
It still points to a future where robots may take over these kinds of business phone calls altogether. Businesses are also experimenting with artificial-intelligence tools to interface with customers, like local California pizza chain Pizza My Heart , which lets you text its Jimmy the Surfer chatbot to order pizza.
It doesn’t seem too far off that you’ll ask your phone to call a restaurant, and the restaurant’s AI will answer. The machines are talking to each other, except they’re just debating whether you want the stuffed crust.

In 2024, Microsoft and Qualcomm kicked off a new category of Windows hardware it called "Copilot+ PCs" that set the baseline for a new wave of AI-first computers, and launched with exclusive features that would not be made available on PCs that didn't meet a new set of system requirements.
The launch didn't go smoothly. Copilot+ PCs were met with immediate backlash from security researchers after discovering that Copilot+ PCs blockbuster feature, Recall, was woefully insecure. This forced the company to delay Recall and ship this new category of devices without its leading AI experience.
This pretty much tarnished the Copilot+ PC brand, and over the last two years more and more OEMs have dropped the moniker from marketing materials and product names. In fact, even Microsoft has seemingly stopped mentioning it.
I've noticed that none of the Surface PCs launched in 2026 include the Copilot+ PC moniker in their product names, unlike the Surface PCs that launched in 2025 and before. Now, you have to go digging to find any mention of Copilot+ compatibility in specification sheets.
At this year's Snapdragon Summit, I had the chance to ask Surface CVP Brett Ostrum about the lack of Copilot+ PC branding on its recent Surface PCs , and he confirmed that " these are not called Copilot+ PCs. They do meet all the requirements of our previous bar for what Copilot+ devices are. We still lean into the narrative around AI on the edge and being able to have a hybrid solution out there."
I've also asked Qualcomm's SVP of compute, Kedar Kondap, about his thoughts on the usage of the Copilot+ PC branding. He told me that "the purpose for Copilot+ PCs was to be able to deliver [NPU] experiences. So it was to define a certain category of devices with a certain bar and metric, like for example, a 45 TOPS NPU ... So from that perspective, it's more offering the same experiences, probably without just using [Copilot+ PC] terminology now. "
It's also worth mentioning that NVIDIA hasn't gone anywhere near the Copilot+ PC brand for its upcoming RTX Spark platform, even though all RTX Spark PCs meet the Copilot+ PC specification bar. I suspect that's a deliberate decision.
It seems pretty obvious that the Copilot+ PC brand hasn't resonated with the market, and OEMs and Microsoft itself are now quietly pulling back on that branding. The specification baseline for Copilot+ PC experiences still exists, it just no longer has a pretty marketing name tied to it.
The rough launch of Copilot+ PCs, paired with the fact that Microsoft Copilot itself doesn't have a very strong reputation these days, likely contributed to the decision to slowly retire the Copilot+ PC branding. The brand never made sense to me anyway... these PCs have nothing to do with Copilot.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that the U.S. and China have reached agreements covering a subset of goods the two countries can trade on more favorable terms, marking fresh progress in negotiations between the world's two largest economies.
"We've actually reached agreement with the Chinese on a number of these things," Greer said on CNBC's "Squawk Box," referring to goods including U.S. agricultural products and medical devices and Chinese consumer goods considered non-sensitive.
Greer said the Trump administration plans to release "a lot more details" Monday about what the two sides have accomplished in negotiations over the past several weeks. He said the goal is to carve out areas of trade that could remain insulated from future tariff measures or broader trade disputes.
The two countries want some goods to be traded on a "more preferential basis" and potentially left aside if either country imposes new tariffs.
Greer did not specify Friday which products are covered by the agreements, how tariffs on those goods could change or when the new terms would take effect. Negotiations under the new U.S.-China "Board of Trade" mechanism are focused on "pure trade issues," Greer said, rather than U.S. national security restrictions on advanced technology.
"All those export controls that are national security issues, we take those off the table," Greer said.
Trump and Xi, after they met in Beijing in May, announced the establishment of the "Board of Trade" to manage trade between the two rivals in non-sensitive products. Businesses have been waiting for more details on what categories of trade would be set aside, under the new framework, for lower tariffs.

Donald Trump couldn’t help but offer guests at his state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping a first-ever tour of his ballroom construction site.
The president loves to boast to the White House press corps and his Truth Social followers about his passion projects around Washington, D.C ., especially the massive White House ballroom being built. Now, in front of an international audience, Trump has offered to share a glimpse of what he called a “clean and sparkly” construction site.
“And if I could go off script just for a second,” Trump said as dinner guests in the East Room of the White House laughed. “But as a special treat in honor of President Xi and Madame [Liyuan] Peng. I'd like to invite everyone in the room to visit through that beautiful curtain in the back.”
“It's one year away from completion — the new ballroom that you've heard about, and you will see something that I think you will really love.”
The 90,000-square-foot golden ballroom will fit 650 seats, compared to the 200 seats in the East Room. Trump has said construction will cost about $400 million and that he and other donors would pay for it.
But the project’s contractor told the administration that it would cost $600 million , with at least half expected to be covered by taxpayers, The Washington Post reported in June.
The Trump administration has also been challenged in court over whether it had the authority to tear down the East Wing last October to build the ballroom without Congressional approval. The Supreme Court ruled last month that the president can continue with construction for the time being .
“You'll be the first people to step foot on that, and we'll do that maybe after we're finished with the entertainment tonight. Anybody [who] wants to walk into a construction site that's nice and clean and sparkly, it's our honor to have you do so,” Trump told his dinner guests.
The official delegations from the US and China attended the state dinner. Some notable names on the guest list included first lady Melania Trump , Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio .
Trump was photographed next to Melania while waiting to greet Xi and his wife Peng at the White House ahead of the dinner. Makeup was caked on his left hand, which he often uses to cover up bruising .
The Trump administration has said the black and blue on the back of his hands is due to frequent handshaking and aspirin use .
Several of America’s tech leaders, such as SpaceX’s Elon Musk , OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg , were also in attendance Thursday night amid an AI race with China .
During the legal fight to build his ballroom, Trump argued that it was needed for national security. Underneath the East Wing sits a bunker dating back to 1942, after the U.S. entered World War II. In court filings, the Trump administration noted that bomb shelters, military installations and a medical facility would be added to the bunker during construction.
So when Trump suggested officials from China, an adversary of the U.S., tour the construction site, it raised some eyebrows.
“Of the security bunker? Seems suboptimal,” Reuters journalist Charlie Szymanski wrote on Bluesky.
“Guided tour of the super secure and classified military ballroom for officials of a foreign unfriendly nation. Totally reasonable,” another Bluesky user, Jeff Domingues, posted .
One X user wrote , “Let’s take the leader of China into the ballroom that doubles as a military bunker! Great idea Don!”
Melania led the preparations for the state dinner, which included a menu that the White House said had a “subtle Chinese influence.” For the main course, guests enjoyed sesame-crusted sea bass and braised baby bok choy.
Entertainment for the night was headlined by Christopher Macchio, a classically trained tenor who performed at Trump’s second inauguration. Guests were also treated to performances by military ensembles.
“Thank you, Mr. President and Mrs. Trump, for extending to my wife and me your gracious hospitality and thoughtful arrangements,” Xi said at the dinner through an interpreter. “You make us feel truly at home.”
“I would also like to extend my sincere greetings to Americans from all sectors of society who care about China-U.S. relations and support the further growth of our bilateral ties.”

articles.title_orig: Trump and Xi exchange warm words at state dinner but little progress on key issues
articles.title_zh: Trump and Xi exchange warm words at state dinner but little progress on key issues
articles.content_orig:
Watch: The worldâs two most powerful men just met. How did it go?
US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping exchanged warm words at a lavish White House state dinner but gave little indication of progress on pressing issues.
Xi stressed that they should ensure AI remain "under human control" and act "as responsible major countries", while Trump toasted a future of "harmony, peace and success" for both nations.
But tensions remain despite the diplomatic niceties, including over Taiwan - with Xi urging Trump earlier in the day to take the "correct position" on the self-governing island which Beijing claims, amid a weapons package paused by Trump.
Billionaire business leaders and US tech CEOs joined the leaders at the extravagant dinner late on Thursday.
Their arrival was marked by protesters shouting from just outside the White House gates, some of whom were arrested.
Trump lavished praise on Xi during his first visit to the US in over a decade, telling those attending the dinner that while the two countries had "different systems", they had "never gotten along better".
Xi meanwhile welcomed the "historic juncture" in US-China relations - and said both leaders' ambitions could "surely be mutually reinforcing".
"China and the United States must act as responsible major countries to meet the expectations of our peoples, keep pace with the trend of our times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other," he said.
While Xi said he and Trump had shared "in-depth exchanges and reached common understanding on many issues", little mention was made of the crucial matters which divide the leaders of the world's two most powerful countries.
China believes the US is trying to contain its rise as a superpower, and it wants Washington to stay out of its way - particularly when it comes to trade, technology and Taiwan.
Trump has meanwhile been expected to aim for deals around trade and tariffs during the visit â like lowering Chinese tariffs on American goods, increasing imports of Chinese rare earth minerals, and increasing exports of US agricultural products.
Xi thanked his hosts for receiving him and his wife with "meticulous care and consideration"
Trump has been blunt about his ambitions for artificial intelligence (AI) - and clear that he considers China to be the US's main rival for its development.
But beyond Xi's reference to AI remaining under "human control", little indication was given of what progress the two leaders may have made on the issue during their talks.
The dinner also came just hours after Chinese state media reported Xi had, behind closed doors, advised Washington to handle "with prudence" its approach to Taiwan. Washington is yet to comment publicly on the remarks.
The US is legally bound to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, but Trump delayed approving a $14bn (Â£11bn) arms package for it after Xi in May warned that mishandling the issue could cause the two countries to "collide or even enter into conflict".
At the time, Trump called it a "very good negotiating chip" with Beijing.
Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far
Trump and Xi come face-to-face as US and China battle to win the AI race
Xi got Trump's red carpet welcome - but not everything he wanted
The evening marked a continuation of the lavish welcome Xi has so far received in the US.
Trump presented the Chinese president with a sculpture of a bald eagle - America's national symbol - saying it embodied "the free and soaring spirit of America". First Lady Melania had participated in its design, Trump added.
Others in attendance included key White House figures, such as Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, chief of staff Monica Crowley, and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.
They were joined by scores of US officials, as well as conservative broadcasters, tech industry bosses, social media CEOs and corporate executives.
Apple's Tim Cook and Nvidia's Jensen Huang were seated at the same table as Trump and Xi, as was Elon Musk, who previously worked in Trump's administration leading the effort to shrink government.
OpenAI's Sam Altman, Google's Sundar Pichai, and Amazon's Jeff Bezos were also present, as were Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Yass, the American billionaire who owns a share of TikTok.
Musk was seen mingling with guests, alongside US Secretary of State Marco Rubio
The leaders of companies including General Motors, Visa, Paramount Skydance and ExxonMobil could also be seen in the room.
"Everybody wanted to be there," Trump said ahead of the event. "I would say you have the entire tech world, the entire banking world, and a lot more."
One notable absence was Anthropic - one of the biggest and most valuable AI firms in the world. The BBC has asked Anthropic if it was invited, or if they chose not to be there.
Business leaders and tech bosses were among those in attendance
The office of the First Lady Melania Trump, which planned the event, said the dinner menu would showcase "American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence".
The first course was yellow squash, wild mushrooms and crispy pancetta. The guests ate off red tablecloths - red being a symbol of luck and good fortune in China.
For their main course they dined on a sesame-crusted sea bass, braised bok choy and roasted eggplant.
Dessert featured the two leaders and their fellow diners tucking into vanilla crÃ©meux with sour cherry confit, with an accompanying ice cream "made with harvested White House honey".
The wine chosen by the first lady included Schramsberg Blanc De Noir - a nod to President Nixon's 1972 "Toast to Peace" with former Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai, when they used a bottle from the same vineyard.
Watch: Trump puts on a warm reception for Xi in Washington
Trump and Xi will begin the final day of their visit on Friday with tea at the White House's Red Room with their wives.
The group will then head to the US National Archives for a tour of the building and its exhibits.
Formally called the National Archives and Records Administration, the building holds some of the most important documents regarding the founding of the United States - including the US Constitution, the Declaration of Independence and the Bill of Rights.
Xi and his wife will depart Washington later in the day.
